lens: Boutique recruiter operational fit: narrow final follow-up on immutable GET-5-product-v3, resolving only the remaining pending-save footer and original-operation recovery dependency. The corrected implementation slice passes with no residual findings. The full-lens verdict remains pass_with_changes, score 2, solely because the unchanged trigger-relevance dimension still lacks a realistic interrupted recruiter task; this is a field-test limit, not a remaining implementation defect or veto.
strengths: Frozen provenance: independently recomputed SHA-256 for all 110 v3 manifest entries; every hash matched. Comparison with v2 finds only the brief, the two pending-footer logs, screenshot 25, RelationshipAskView.swift and CandidateSignalUITests.swift changed or added. Direct source diffs contain only the pending-footer branch/icon/accessibility correction and native test setup/assertions. Other behavior and v2 evidence are carried forward unchanged. No other specialist packet or score was read.

Resolved v1 finding 2 / interruption recovery = 3/4: the fork is visibly labeled “Fork”, and its accessibility label says “Forked Session”, while the original retains its original title and history. Direct proof: /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/screenshots/16-fork-label-v2.png; /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/source/apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveView.swift:3554-3574 and :3672-3682; /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/source/apps/ios/UITests/Get5SessionUITests.swift:67-91; /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/get5-ios-ui-panel2-r1.log:1504. The persistent field is originSessionID, not a transient toast. The exact two-branch next-day field task remains unobserved.

Resolved final v2 residual / write safety = 3/4. The footer now prioritizes hasPendingWrite with no receipt and uses the truthful unknown-save text; its icon and combined accessibility label match that state. Direct source: /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/source/apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipAskView.swift:5733-5752. Direct rendered proof: /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/screenshots/25-pending-footer-v3.png shows the whole recovery card, including the footer below Retry same operation, and contains no proposal-only/nothing-changes assurance. The actual after-commit response-loss test explicitly reveals the footer and checks its unknown wording (/tmp/get5-product-review-v3/source/apps/ios/UITests/CandidateSignalUITests.swift:5047-5055; /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/get5-ios-ui-pending-footer-r8.log:297-316). The same test then relaunches, retries the original operation and restores the original Session/source/receipt with a working People destination; it passes at :592-606 in 96.407 seconds. The preceding r7 remains a failed startup run. No original-operation behavior changed in the v3 implementation diff.

State integrity = 3/4. The authenticated canonical app case deliberately creates Noor Vega, restarts, retains one Session with the exact original source and a receipt, previews shared deletion scope, cancels deletion, and reopens the same receipt. /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/source/apps/ios/UITests/Get5CanonicalSessionUITests.swift:14-91; /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/get5-ios-ui-canonical-panel2-r5.log:426; /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/screenshots/22-authenticated-delete-scope-v2.png and screenshots/23-authenticated-session-source-receipt-v2.png. This proves authenticated single-Simulator task completion and deletion cancellation; it does not prove deletion propagation on a second phone.

Capture burden = 3/4, retained from the unchanged bounded capture review. Natural name/email input stages a draft, and deterministic voice remains editable without sending; text/hold/tap controls have recorded native passes. /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/conversation-provider-proof.json:153-246; /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/get5-ios-ui-final-r6.log:1012, :1060 and :1330; /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/screenshots/02-voice-draft.png. Total user effort versus manual entry and actual transcription accuracy remain unmeasured.

Evidence review = 3/4. The draft retains an inspectable source and field excerpts; incomplete relationship context disables saving and can be declined while the message survives. /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/source/apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipAskView.swift:5552-5567 and :5762-5778; /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/get5-ios-ui-final-r6.log:1287. The previously incomplete native screenshot source/detail/follow-up test now has a passing individual result at /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/get5-ios-ui-final-r8.log:372. This is a deterministic screenshot fixture, separately supported by the actual-provider tests below.

Action usefulness = 3/4 for the bounded contact job. Saving yields a receipt and a working People destination in the authenticated recovery trace (/tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/get5-ios-ui-authenticated-recovery-r6.log:540-561). In two final configured GLM trials, “What does Friday mean?” uses existing canonical screenshot context, keeps date/timezone uncertainty, and suggests checking existing capture or asking for the missing timing; it does not demand a duplicate screenshot upload. /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/screenshot-provider-proof.v3.json:46-179 and :182-355. These are two observed answers, not a reliability or candidate-momentum outcome estimate.

Wedge discipline = 3/4. The affected corrections improve ordinary retrieval and review without adding unrelated features. The screenshot follow-up is explicitly proposed/unconfirmed and carries no formal write in both final trials (/tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/screenshot-provider-proof.v3.json:162-179 and :338-355). The shared deletion preview states the scope and says saved contacts and other Sessions stay unchanged (/tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/screenshots/22-authenticated-delete-scope-v2.png). No person scoring is visible in the affected surfaces.

Additional bounded dependency proof: /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/backend-clock-after.log:92-95 records 87/87 final affected tests. /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/backend-proof.v2.json:6-12 identifies 42 PostgreSQL Session cases and 34 provider cases. This closes the v1 absence of an inspectable final backend log; it does not convert a provider response or database test into field usefulness.

Affected-slice completion: both original implementation findings are resolved—persistent fork identity was verified in v2 and remains unchanged, and truthful pending-save communication is now directly verified across the full visible card in v3. Findings and vetoes are empty. Remaining rubric scores retain the v2 calibration: trigger relevance 2; capture burden 3; evidence review 3; state integrity 3; action usefulness 3; write safety now 3; interruption recovery 3; wedge discipline 3. The reported score is the minimum material dimension, not an average.
missing_evidence: Trigger relevance remains 2/4. The v2 brief retains a plausible recent-conversation task but no concrete active-search count, decision deadline or competing task. The same unconfirmed Friday scenario is useful for continuity but is not a realistic urgency/attention study. Add one interrupted recruiter search task with an explicit commitment before claiming complete operational fit. This is a research/test gap, not a demonstrated product failure.

Field-value hypothesis remains open: no recruiter observation establishes lower effort than copying a note/manual contact entry, reliable detection of seeded identity/purpose errors, fewer missed commitments, or improved outcomes. A moderated comparison should measure source checking, correction burden, total task time and return-to-task accuracy. No score of 4 or field-usefulness claim is awarded.

The authenticated native proof uses one Simulator and a loopback simulated-login/keychain bridge. It does not exercise two actual phones, next-day return, changed external contact state, or physical-device VoiceOver. The deletion test previews and cancels; it does not itself demonstrate actual multi-device deletion. These are scope limits, not evidence that sync/deletion fails.

The fork label is directly visible and accessible after the native edge-back journey, but the exact v1 proposed verification with different subsequent messages in both branches and a later restart was not performed in that UI test. Existing persisted origin identity supports the correction; cross-day retrieval effectiveness is still inferred.

The unreattachable-original-images case from v1 remains untested. The existing recovery gate preserves the original task and avoids text replay; this packet does not infer that removing the gate is safe.

Native proof is cumulative: the canonical case passes at /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/get5-ios-ui-canonical-panel2-r5.log:426, but that file also contains a failed recovery case and ends TEST FAILED. The recovery is separately green at /tmp/get5-product-review-v3/evidence/get5-ios-ui-authenticated-recovery-r6.log:561-575. Likewise only the screenshot case is credited in final-r8, and only the specified fork/AX5 cases in panel2-r1. No single all-green native suite is claimed.

The old general conversation provider trial remains a bounded continuity example that writes from applicant to recruiter after an ambiguous prompt. The new screenshot trials demonstrate a narrower useful clarification, not an explicit recruiter-to-candidate outreach task. Production parity, deployment, TestFlight distribution and physical-device proof remain with root and are not asserted here.

The final footer assertion is directly executed before relaunch; after relaunch the existing protected-operation, original-source, receipt and People-readback checks execute. The same deterministic footer branch applies to restored pending state, but no second post-relaunch footer screenshot is included. This does not leave a reproduced defect. Physical-device/field proof, final incremental Release validation and deployment remain outside this packet.
